hypothesis: Eliminate a frequent scalar class-formation tree by changing the scalar origin: sum(s_i P_i)=c*S+sum((s_i-c)P_i), S=sum(P_i). S is a single key-only aggregate point per query, not a lookup table. Choose c as the most frequent scalar (zero wins ties) so grouping skips c instead of zero.
distinction: Prior opposite-scalar census reduces only1/3primaryA/B unique classes. This examines occurrence counts of the largest class, potentially removing many fresh grouping point additions with O(1) retained key points. It does not repeat window-pair reuse, lookup tables or signed-radix precomputation.
scope: Read-only population and operation-count model in nine actual fresh accepted-library A/B scalar vectors. RawK is diagnostic, not foldedK/EulerH. Cached and raw solver outputs must agree. No candidate point code, timing gain or new proof.
model: For each exact scalar class count frequency. Old class-formation additions=sum(count-1) over nonzero classes. Translated additions=sum(count-1) over classes except c; add one output correction point and account separately for its variable scalar multiplication. Key sum setup requires n-1 modeled additions once. Changed scalar window work and exceptional curve cases are unmodeled. One constant point per queried vector is the proposed persistent storage; preparation must later stream in bounded scratch and preserve fallback under denied admission.
validation: Two independent deterministic weighted Fr functionals verify c*sum(weights)+sum((s-c)*class_weight_sum)==sum(s*weight), with every original row assigned exactly once. Synthetic allzero,allone,mixed/random,zero-dominant populations. No scalar/witness arrays or private scalar values exported; mode tag restricted to zero/one/minusone/other.
decision: If mode is zero or modeled reduction cannot justify prep/transform/correction costs, stop before point implementation. Otherwise implement separately declared real caller test with independently checked curve outputs and complete timing including fresh grouping/translation/correction. No speed inference from counts or arbitrary minimum positive gain floor.
